stage_2_story.text_en:
On Saturday afternoon, Avi decided it was finally time to fix a few things around the house that had been bothering him for weeks. He carried his toolbox from the storage room to the living room and set it on the floor.

The first job was to hang a large family photo on the wall. Avi picked up his tape measure and marked the exact spot on the wall where he wanted the nail to go. Then he checked the mark with his level to make sure the picture would hang straight. Satisfied, he grabbed his hammer and drove the nail firmly into the wall. The photo looked perfect.

Next, Avi moved to the kitchen. The cabinet door had a loose hinge with two screws that kept falling out. He found the right screwdriver in his toolbox and tightened both screws carefully. The door swung smoothly again.

After that, he went to the balcony where a wooden bench had been sitting unfinished for a month. The surface was rough, so he spent fifteen minutes rubbing it with sandpaper until it was completely smooth. Then he used his drill to make four holes for the bolts that would hold the bench legs firmly in place. He tightened the bolts with his wrench.

Before cutting a wooden strip to cover the gap under the balcony door, Avi measured the length with his tape measure twice. Then he clamped the wood to the table and cut it cleanly with his saw. He even used his pliers to remove a small bent nail that was sticking out of the wood.

By evening, Avi had fixed everything on his list. He packed all his tools neatly back into the toolbox and called his son. "Come see — I fixed the bench, the cabinet, and the photo," he said proudly. His son looked around and said, "Dad, you should have been a carpenter."
